title: Banana Walnut Muffins with a Demerara Top
changes_from_base: Mashed ripe banana replaces the buttermilk and berries, oil replaces the butter, and toasted walnuts with demerara go on top.
summary: Moist banana muffins full of toasted walnuts, with a crackly demerara top.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan) and grease the tin. Whisk the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt in a medium bowl.

steps.title: Banana
steps.text: Mash the bananas in a large bowl with a fork until mostly smooth. Whisk in the light brown sugar, eggs, oil and vanilla.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the flour mix and whisk just until no dry patches remain, then stir in about three-quarters of the toasted walnuts.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Divide between the 12 holes; they will be very full. Scatter the rest of the walnuts and the demerara over the tops.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 14-18 min, until the tops are deep golden and a cocktail stick comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Leave in the tin for 10 min, then move to the rack for at least 5 min before eating.

tips: The most common mistake is using bananas that are only just yellow; they need lots of brown spots for flavour and moisture.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 4-5 min until fragrant.
For nut-free muffins leave out the walnuts and scatter a few rolled oats with the demerara instead.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep in an airtight box at room temperature for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
